metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: Change AC#4 to enforce a KEY-SET invariant (no baseline key present now may be absent on main's baseline) rather than a count-only comparison, so a new entry cannot be masked by removing an unrelated one.
evidence: AC#4: 'A test asserts the baseline entry count is monotonically non-increasing against main'
AC#5: 'Adding a new function above the C901 threshold fails CI even when a matching baseline entry is added in the same change'
Codebase: baseline is a keyed map (`.github/complexity-baseline.json` `ceilings` object); the natural invariant is over the KEY SET, not cardinality
test_complexity_baseline.py only checks `len(ceilings) == live` — count, not membership
findings.finding: AC#4's chosen mechanism (assert entry count is monotonically non-increasing against main) is a proxy strictly weaker than the goal AC#5 names (a new function above C901 must fail even if a matching baseline entry is added). A change that removes >=1 existing entry while adding a new high-complexity entry keeps the count flat-or-lower yet admits new debt.
scenarios: Contributor refactors function A below threshold (entry removed, count -1) and in the same change adds a genuinely new function B above threshold (entry added, count +1): net count unchanged, monotonic-non-increasing check passes, new debt admitted
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the committed baseline's key set is a subset of main's baseline key set (new keys forbidden; removals allowed), which is strictly stronger than count monotonicity and directly satisfies AC#5 while still permitting shrinkage (AC#6).

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile AC#1 and AC#6 by specifying that the lock gates only GROWTH (new keys and/or raised ceilings), not any file diff, so shrinkage passes while growth requires an override.
evidence: AC#1: 'a change to the file fails the build unless an administrator overrides the gate, matching the module-size limit's posture'
_build-and-test.yml:367-369 module-size lock errors on ANY difference: `if [ "$BASE" != "$LIMIT" ]; then ... exit 1`
AC#6: 'Legitimate baseline SHRINKAGE (a function refactored below its ceiling, entry removed) still passes without an override'
findings.finding: AC#1 (lock the file so any change requires an administrator override, 'matching the module-size limit's posture' — which errors on ANY diff) directly conflicts with AC#6 (legitimate shrinkage with an entry removed must pass WITHOUT an override). A whole-file diff-lock like the module-size gate would block shrinkage, which is itself a file change.
scenarios: A contributor removes a ceiling entry (shrinkage): under a module-size-style whole-file lock the file differs from main and the gate errors, contradicting AC#6
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe AC#1: the lock fails only on a growth diff (new key or increased ceiling vs. main), not on any change; shrinkage (removed key / lowered ceiling) passes without an override, and the fail-closed rule applies when main's baseline cannot be fetched.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving step that exercises the fetch-failure branch (e.g. point the base ref at a non-existent remote/ref, or inject an empty base value) and asserts the job exits non-zero for BOTH the complexity-baseline lock and the fixed module-size lock.
evidence: AC: 'The lock FAILS CLOSED when the base value cannot be fetched — no ::warning::-and-continue'
No step or test in the plan simulates a fetch failure or asserts the exit code of the fail-closed path
findings.finding: The AC 'The lock FAILS CLOSED when the base value cannot be fetched' has no described proving mechanism. Simulating a git-fetch-of-main failure in CI is non-trivial, and the plan names no test, fixture, or command that exercises the fetch-failure branch. Without one, the fail-closed behavior is asserted but unverified — the same class of latent bug the plan is fixing in the module-size lock.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'The lock FAILS CLOSED when the base value cannot be fetched'
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the base-value fetch into a script whose failure path is unit-testable, and add a test that runs it with an unreachable ref and asserts a non-zero exit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a bounded retry/backoff on the base-value fetch before failing closed, so a single transient fetch flake does not hard-block every build; document the retry count.
evidence: Plan: 'if the git fetch of main fails, the lock emits ::warning:: and skips'
Plan acknowledges flakiness: 'passes on any run where that fetch flakes'
New requirement: 'must fail CLOSED when it cannot establish the base value'
findings.finding: Mandating fail-closed on git-fetch-of-main failure introduces a new build-blocking failure mode without discussing transient-flake handling. The plan itself notes the current lock skips comparison 'if the git fetch of main fails' precisely because that fetch can flake ('any run where that fetch flakes'). Switching to fail-closed means every transient fetch flake now hard-blocks unrelated PRs, with no retry/backoff described.
findings.location: 'Do NOT copy the module-size lock's fail-open' section
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small retry (e.g. 3 attempts with backoff) around the git fetch; fail closed only after retries are exhausted.

evidence: verify command `grep 'complexity-baseline' .github/workflows/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: No file_impact declared on a leaf work ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the {path, reason} files this work will touch (e.g. via set_file_impact) so the attestation is scoped to them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete documentation location (e.g. a sibling .github/complexity-baseline.README.md or an AGENTS.md section) rather than 'next to the file'.
evidence: AC: 'The intended posture — who may change the baseline and how — is documented next to the file'
JSON files admit no comments, so 'next to' cannot mean inline
findings.finding: The AC 'The intended posture ... is documented next to the file' does not fix a documentation location, and .github/complexity-baseline.json is JSON, which cannot carry inline comments. 'Next to the file' is ambiguous — a sibling README, an AGENTS.md entry, or a workflow comment are materially different homes and the executor must guess.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'The intended posture ... is documented next to the file'
findings.suggested_fix: Name a specific file, e.g. '.github/complexity-baseline.README.md documenting the administrator-only, shrink-only posture'.
